title: Budget and Revenue
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Films with bigger budgets tend to earn more worldwide, as Figure 1 shows.

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (million USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Budget against worldwide revenue (millions of USD)

This site explores films.csv, a dataset of 104 well-known films released between 1980 and 2025. For each film it records the budget, worldwide revenue, runtime and IMDb rating. Figures are rounded and not adjusted for inflation.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Figure 1 shows whether longer films get higher ratings.

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime against IMDb rating





Mean rating by decade:

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

The dataset covers Bond films from 1995 to 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of the Bond films over time
